notes: Intent rules for the group acquisition flow.
Patterns are ordinary Python regular expressions and are matched against
NORMALISED text (see app/intent.py). Write them in normal Persian: the
engine runs the same character unification over the patterns, so you do
not have to think about Arabic yeh/kaf, ZWNJ or Persian digits here.
Use \s* between the words of a phrase so one pattern covers 'فیلترشکن',
'فیلتر شکن' and 'فیلتر  شکن'. Whitespace is already collapsed to single
spaces before matching, and ZWNJ is removed, so 'ک ب نت', 'ک‌ب‌نت' and
'کب نت' are all the same string by the time a pattern sees them.
The engine folds Arabic/Persian letter forms and digits in the patterns
too, and that includes punctuation: a Persian question mark becomes '?',
so a pattern that wants a literal question mark must escape it as \?.
How a message is judged:
* topic + at least one of (request, problem, poor_internet)  -> intent
* any standalone pattern                                     -> intent
* any ignore pattern                                         -> never
* otherwise                                                  -> not an intent
A bare mention of a VPN with no request and no complaint is NOT intent,
which is what keeps ordinary chatter in the group from triggering.
ai_candidates is different from every other group and it is weight 0:
it never makes a message an intent and it never vetoes one. It only marks
a message as worth a second opinion from the AI layer (app/ai_intent.py),
which is consulted when the rules are unsure. Keep it LOOSE - it is a
plausibility gate, not evidence - but not so loose that everyday words
('لینک', 'بدون', 'بسته') spend a Gemini call each. Set 'candidate_group'
to point at a different group name, or leave the group out entirely to
switch the escalation off.
To extend: add patterns to a group. To add a new kind of supporting
signal, add a group under 'groups' with weight 1 and list its name in
'support_groups'. To change the balance, change 'topic_groups'.

topic.comment: Signals that the message is about circumvention. Alone they prove nothing.

request.comment: Signals that the user wants something. Supporting signal only.

problem.comment: Signals that something is broken. Supporting signal only.

comment: Complaints about connectivity in general. On their own they are NOT
enough — half the group complains about slow internet — so they only
count when the message is also about circumvention.
The mobile operators are here rather than in 'topic' because naming
your ISP is not a statement about circumvention: 'ایرانسل وصل نمیشه'
is a person whose connection is bad, who may or may not be looking for
a way around it. The AI layer gets to weigh that one.
WEIGHT 0 — the plausibility gate for the AI layer, and nothing else.
It cannot make a message an intent and it cannot veto one. When the
rules are unsure, a hit here is what makes the message worth one
Gemini call (app/classifier.py); a miss means the rules' silence is
taken as final and no call is spent.
Pricing words are here on purpose. In this group 'قیمتتون چنده' is
almost always about our own service, and 'قیمت گوشی چنده' is not — and
telling those apart is the model's job, not a rule's. Both spend one
call; the model decides which one is a lead.
It is deliberately looser than 'topic' — blocked services, operator
names, connectivity words — because the whole point is to catch the
phrasings no rule was written for. It is also deliberately not as
loose as 'every word about the internet': 'لینک', 'بدون' and 'بسته'
are common enough in ordinary group chatter that a call each would be
a waste of the daily quota.
Phrases that are unambiguous on their own: someone asking how to get
past a block without naming a tool. Keep this list tight — every entry
here bypasses the topic requirement.
Hard vetoes, checked first. A competing seller advertising in the group
is not a customer, and answering them with a trial link is noise.
A veto is final on purpose: the AI layer is never consulted for a message
that lands here, so no amount of prompt-shaped persuasion can talk the
bot into advertising at a competitor.
Every pattern names a selling act. 'میفروشم' is first person, so a
customer asking 'کسی میفروشه؟' is not caught by it.
